beats.text: When your friend gets happier, you probably do too.
Researchers followed almost five thousand people for twenty years.
Each house is one person. This is you. This is a friend nearby.
When that friend got happier, your chance of being happy went up by twenty-five percent.
And it spread up to three steps. To friends of friends of friends.
Your mood travels further than you think. That's why

sources: Fowler & Christakis (2008), Dynamic spread of happiness in a large social network: longitudinal analysis over 20 years in the Framingham Heart Study, BMJ 337:a2338 – 4,739 people followed 1983–2003; a friend living within a mile who becomes happy increases the probability that a person is happy by about 25 % (95 % CI 1–57 %); next-door neighbours 34 %, siblings within a mile 14 %, spouse 8 %; clusters of happiness extend up to three degrees of separation (observational; the contagion interpretation is debated).
